statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Coronaviruses that recognize the same host receptor also cause comparable disease severity in those hosts.
statements.evidence: coronaviruses from different genera being able to recognize the same receptor and coronaviruses from the same genus able to bind distinct receptors
statements.note: The abstract describes shared and distinct receptor recognition across genera but says nothing about disease severity in the hosts.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Several changes in the S protein reduced antibody neutralization activity while altering receptor-binding affinity.
statements.evidence: many changes in the S protein have been under positive selection by altering the receptor-binding affinity, reducing antibody neutralization activities
statements.note: The abstract states these S protein changes reduced antibody neutralization activity and altered receptor-binding affinity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Signals of positive selection in the S1 N-terminal domain appeared in pairwise comparisons across all four coronavirus genera.
statements.evidence: the S1 N-terminal domain exhibits signals of positive selection in the pairwise comparisons in all four coronavirus genera
statements.note: The abstract reports positive selection signals in the S1 N-terminal domain across all four coronavirus genera.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Positive selection acted on the S gene, especially the S1 region, in both SARS-CoV-2 and the other coronaviruses examined.
statements.evidence: the S gene, particularly the S1 region, has experienced positive selection in both SARS-CoV-2 and other coronaviruses
statements.note: The abstract reports the S gene, especially S1, underwent positive selection in SARS-CoV-2 and other coronaviruses alike.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Splice-disrupting variants underwent greater purifying selection in anatomically modern humans than in Neanderthals.
statements.evidence: splice-disrupting variants experienced greater purifying selection in anatomically modern humans than that in Neanderthals
statements.note: The abstract reports greater purifying selection on splice-disrupting variants in anatomically modern humans than in Neanderthals.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The MaPSy assay tested 5,169 alleles and uncovered 962 exonic splicing mutations distinguishing extant from extinct hominins.
statements.evidence: Of the 5,169 alleles tested in this massively parallel splicing reporter assay (MaPSy), we report 962 exonic splicing mutations that correspond to differences in exon recognition between extant and extinct hominins
statements.note: The abstract reports 962 exonic splicing mutations among 5,169 tested alleles, reflecting exon-recognition differences between extant and extinct hominins.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: After introgression, adaptively acquired variants were enriched for moderate-effect splicing variants.
statements.evidence: Adaptively introgressed variants were enriched for moderate-effect splicing variants
statements.note: The abstract reports adaptively introgressed variants were enriched for splicing variants of moderate effect.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The pathogenic splicing variants limited to Neanderthals and Denisovans drove these hominins to extinction.
statements.evidence: We further identified potentially pathogenic splicing variants found only in Neanderthals and Denisovans in genes related to sperm maturation and immunity
statements.note: The abstract reports these variants only in Neanderthals and Denisovans and, separately, that the hominins went extinct, but never links the two.
